No, not yet. WSL2 supports the sandbox, but only when both of its packages are installed: bubblewrap and socat. Your `command -v socat` came back empty, so the sandbox backend is not available on this machine as it stands.

That matters because granting Bash puts every command under the sandbox. With no working backend the CLI refuses each run that grants Bash instead of running it unconfined, so that case reports a run error and usually scores 0. You would pay for runs that measure nothing.

Install socat (`sudo apt-get install socat`), restart Claude Code, and run `/sandbox` to confirm there is no Dependencies tab. Then pay for the run.

Without socat the sandbox can't come up, and the eval CLI rejects every run in which Bash is allowed rather than letting it execute unprotected. Those runs come back as errors worth zero.

Add the socat package with your distribution's package manager, relaunch Claude Code, and then the Bash case can actually be measured.

Not quite. The preflight would report `sandbox_backend: absent (missing: socat)`. WSL2 uses the same sandbox as Linux, which needs bubblewrap and socat; bwrap resolves but socat does not, so each run that grants Bash is refused and usually scores 0 rather than running unconfined.

Install socat and restart before paying.

Two extras: on Ubuntu 24.04 and later, also check `sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`, since an AppArmor restriction can stop bwrap even with both installed. And your read-only cases are unaffected either way.
